newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares edge up on steady support - traders.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares edge up on steady support - traders.

text.p: Leading Russian shares rose slightly on Monday but traders did not see significant change in the market in the near future as second-tier shares continued to attract most investor demand.
The Russian Trading System index of 22 shares closed at 365.64, up slightly from 360.94 on Monday, on an unexceptional $32.4 million overall market turnover.
"So far all the movement in "blue chips" is due exclusively to individual orders -- no one is doing any global buying," said ING Bank trader Oleg Galkin.
"The market is weakly, step-by-step, moving upwards, purely out of inertia in my view."
But traders noted Russian investors supporting the market in morning trade, and said foreign demand became noticeable during the day.
"In my view the market has got good support," said Renaissance Capital trader Vladimir Chkikvadze.
Galkin said metals mining concern Norilsk Nickel and oil company Surgutneftegaz were still enjoying demand left over from Friday, although near record levels were making many wary.
National savings bank Sberbank SBER.RTS continued its rise of recent days, rising to $196.00 from $194.00.
